claims.text: The starting material is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder produced by gas atomization or a similar powder-fabrication method.
The proposed intervention is controlled build-platform preheating during laser powder bed fusion.
Build-platform preheating will reduce thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients will produce a more uniform grain structure.
Reduced thermal gradients will lessen elemental segregation.
Reduced thermal gradients will lessen defect nucleation at grain boundaries.
Elevating the substrate temperature moderates the cooling rate during LPBF solidification.
A moderated cooling rate minimizes solidification-induced compositional gradients.
A moderated cooling rate reduces thermal-stress and residual-stress buildup.
Substrate preheating limits LPBF defects such as microcracks and voids.
Relative to room-temperature LPBF AlCrFeNiSi, preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will have less compositional segregation.
Relative to room-temperature LPBF AlCrFeNiSi, preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress.
Relative to room-temperature LPBF AlCrFeNiSi, preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will contain fewer processing defects.
Preheated LPBF AlCrFeNiSi will exhibit increased toughness and ductility while retaining high strength.
Room-temperature LPBF AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits notable segregation.
Room-temperature LPBF AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits high thermal stresses and associated defects that compromise mechanical integrity.
The proposed effect is valid only within a preheat-temperature window that avoids unwanted phase transformations while preserving complete melting and rapid solidification.
The optimum preheat temperature may depend on laser parameters, powder morphology, and atmospheric conditions.
Segregation, residual stress, strength, and ductility can be compared between room-temperature and preheated LPBF samples to test the hypothesis.
